why: Targets are RANGES with a rationale, never a single pulled-from-air multiplier. Ranges are set so a red gate means a real regression: the machine-independent metrics (success_rate, unresolved) carry the hard budget, and the timing/memory ranges are wide enough to survive a different CI runner while still catching a catastrophic (multi-x) regression.

measured_baseline.note: Two back-to-back runs agreed exactly on success_rate/unresolved and within 2.4% on timing.

success_rate.rationale: 51 of 58 examples/*.tl type-check clean; the 7 that do not are intentionally non-checking. A drop below 0.85 is a parser/checker regression, not example churn. Machine-independent.

unresolved.rationale: Companion to success_rate (files that fail to check). Baseline 7; headroom to 12 before the range trips.

check_ms_median.rationale: Baseline 13.0 ms on aarch64/8-vCPU. The range guards a >4x regression; the precise budget lives in the gate (15%), because a shared CI runner cannot resolve 5%.

check_ms_p95.rationale: Baseline 16.6 ms. Same reasoning as the median.

throughput_files_per_s.rationale: Baseline 10.8 files/s single-threaded; range guards a >4x collapse.

peak_rss_mb.rationale: Baseline 23.3 MB. Range guards an order-of-magnitude memory regression.

notes: Corpus is examples/*.tl: real programs the checker is meant to accept. stdlib/*.tl is NOT the corpus — only 11 of 85 pass 'tallow check' standalone, because the stdlib decls use constructs the standalone checker does not parse (await, _, method-call syntax). That is recorded, not opened, and is a separate item.

The gate's machine-independent checks (success_rate, unresolved) block on any runner. The precise same-machine regression comparison runs where the machine is stable (this aarch64 box / a nightly lane), not on a shared CI runner.
